game_build_reference: Primary sources: (1) Kaivax Blizzard dev notes, us.forums.blizzard.com thread 2360696 post #6, posted 2026-10-16T00:15:00 (WoW Forever Beta Development Notes - Updated October 15) -- does not mention Warlock spell coefficients, Demonic Sacrifice, or Demonic Pact. (2) Official Blizzard blue post 'World of Warcraft: Forever Class Deep Dives -- Rogue and Warlock', mirrored by Wowhead's Blue Tracker, found 2026-10-17 -- CONFIRMS the exact Demonic Sacrifice/Demonic Pact rule this pack had already adopted as its best-sourced candidate (see disputed_mechanics and dispute_ledger below, now resolved). REV2 (2026-10-17): corrected after a user-identified methodology flaw -- single-pass Wowhead-tooltip-widget extraction (via an AI-summarized page fetch) was found to systematically collapse real min-max damage ranges into single, sometimes outright wrong, values (Immolate's original 9-direct-damage figure was almost certainly an extraction error, not real data -- see the Immolate entry's source note). Re-sourced via multiple independent WebSearch passes, which proved more reliable at preserving quoted ranges than fetching Wowhead's own rendered tooltip page. Confidence tags across this pack are demoted from the prior revision's `beta-datamine` to `community-reported` to reflect what these values actually are: web-research-synthesized, not self-extracted or primary-confirmed. See docs/PLAN.md's data-sourcing investigation and plan for the full writeup, including why Wowhead has no usable public API and why wago.tools (direct DB2 extraction) is the recommended path to real `beta-datamine`-tier confidence going forward. REV3 (2026-10-17): the REV2 WebSearch-synthesized ranges were themselves wrong. Found a genuinely structured source, thewowdb.com/wow-forever/ -- directly accessible (unlike Wowhead, which blocks plain HTTP with a 403), and each spell page states explicitly 'Generated from the SpellEffect, SpellMisc, SpellCooldowns and SpellRange records in the WoW Forever beta client, build 1.60.1.70450' with a consistent 'Effect #N ... Value: X Spell power coefficient: Y' structure across every spell checked. None of Shadow Bolt, Corruption, Immolate, Shadowburn, or Searing Pain (the user's own original example) show any die-sides/range field anywhere on their detail pages or in a full-text scan for an 'X to Y' pattern -- strong evidence WoW Forever's redesign gave these direct-damage caster spells flat, non-random base values, not Classic-style rolled ranges. Confidence raised to beta-datamine for every entry below, since this is genuine, consistently-formatted client-data extraction, not web-research synthesis -- still short of live-confirmed since this is beta, not live, data.

disputed_mechanics.name: Demonic Sacrifice interaction with Demonic Pact
disputed_mechanics.description: RESOLVED 2026-10-17 by a primary source. Demonic Sacrifice's own base tooltip (classicwowforever.com) says plainly: 'The effect is canceled if any Demon is summoned' -- undisputed without the Demonic Pact talent. This pack had already adopted a same-pet-vs-different-pet-exemption rule as its best-sourced candidate, based on wofwforever.com's quote of Demonic Pact's tooltip. That rule is now CONFIRMED by an official Blizzard blue post, 'World of Warcraft: Forever Class Deep Dives -- Rogue and Warlock' (mirrored by Wowhead's Blue Tracker, found 2026-10-17; see this pack's game_build_reference): 'Your Demonic Sacrifice effect is no longer cancelled by summoning a different pet. Resummoning the sacrificed pet will still cancel the effect.' The post also confirms Demonic Pact requires the Soul Link talent as a prerequisite, and that it is the 31-point gold medal talent in Demonology. The alternative candidate rule below (the original, cruder framing with no same-pet exception) is kept in the record rather than deleted, per Plan Section 4.7 -- it is now contradicted by a primary source, not merely 'the other guess.'

candidate_rules.label: Demonic Pact exempts a different-pet resummon only; resummoning the sacrificed pet still cancels it

source.name: Official Blizzard blue post, 'World of Warcraft: Forever Class Deep Dives -- Rogue and Warlock' (via Wowhead Blue Tracker)

candidate_rules.description: Confirmed Demonic Pact tooltip: 'Your Demonic Sacrifice effect is no longer cancelled by summoning a different pet. Resummoning the sacrificed pet will still cancel the effect.' (Also corroborated pre-confirmation by wofwforever.com's independent quote of the same tooltip.)

candidate_rules.label: Demonic Pact exempts any resummon, including the sacrificed pet itself
candidate_rules.description: Original framing: 'Demonic Pact lifted the old restriction: the sacrificed bonus stays as long as you summon a different demon.' Did not mention or rule out a same-pet exception either way; now contradicted by the primary source above rather than merely a competing guess.
